newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MARK, YEN, DLR REVIVE HUNGARY BCE FX FUTURES MKT.
newsitem.headline: MARK, YEN, DLR REVIVE HUNGARY BCE FX FUTURES MKT.

text.p: Rising mark, mixed yen and easing dollar futures boosted turnover on the financial section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange, traders said on Monday.
"Closing of speculative positions was behind most of the mark deals," said Janos Mladoniczky of Futures Broker.
September, the only traded mark position, rose 0.40 to 112.60 forints and accounted for 10,418 contracts out of a total 27,343 lots.
September was also popular for the yen, which finished 0.20 lower at 155.35 forints per 100 yen and the other traded maturity, December rose 0.20 to 162.00 forints.
Mladoniczky said some players took a wait-and-see attitude about the yen while others sought to close positions.
Dollar trading was enlivened by the U.S. unit's movements on spot markets and all traded maturities finished lower on Monday.
June went down 0.53 to 184.12 forints, one forint for both September and December to 190.50 and 196 forints, respectively.
The central bank quoted the three currencies in its midday fix at 105.48 forints to the mark, up 0.35, 179.65 for the dollar, down 0.79, and 143.28 per 100 yen, down 0.02.
Total turnover of foreign currency futures on the BCE was 4.17 billion forints, up from Friday's 1.44 million.
